threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'London Fields' instead of ‘Fields’ – that’s a dead giveaway. Locals keep it short, and they never say ‘London’ twice.
Last night on the 35, a guy pulled out a ukulele and started singing a mash-up of Adele and Bob Marley. Everyone just went quiet, then joined in.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw the guy in the corner café ordering a currywurst with a side of vegan kale chips. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice the random techno parties in abandoned buildings? Only in Kreuzberg will you dance in a crumbling kitchen while wearing a wig and a tutu.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know to avoid 16th St BART during rush hour—it's like a parade of lost tourists every time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I watched a group of tourists try to convince a Muni driver to let them on after the bus was full. The driver just shook his head and pulled away.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss the small, local bakeries tucked away. There’s nothing like a morning xuxo from a corner shop—definitely not the same as La Rambla!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll find them scrutinizing the metro map like it's written in hieroglyphics, while locals zip past without a glance.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver shouts 'next stop' like it’s a game show, while locals jump off at random without a thought.
Caught a night bus in Brixton, and a guy was arguing with a post about the Tube strikes like it was a person. Even the bus driver was nodding in agreement.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids using an old bike as a makeshift table for their chess game outside a Späti. That’s just Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only here do you find a Kebab shop that doubles as a gallery. Past the döner counter, art hangs on the walls, and locals gather to discuss both.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they nonchalantly navigate BART delays while the newcomers panic. We've all learned to expect the unexpected here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that had to stop for a guy selling fresh flowers on the corner. Only in San Francisco do we turn transit delays into mini markets.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just for the parks and squares, but the real charm is in the back streets where the old shops sell things no one else does.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their struggle to find a place that serves proper fricandó—it’s like a rite of passage here.
